sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:7
items.html:
Twelve kinds of reflected light; the reflected light that in its totality is rejected from Malchut becomes surrounding light
Twelve kinds of reflected light we find here in the ARI’s words, and these are they:
The first is the reflected light rejected from phase four at the time of the first look, when the screen restrains the upper light and does not let it expand there, and the light returns backwards and clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light, as is known. Now there are two kinds of reflected light to be understood here. The first is the totality of the light rejected from clothing in the vessel of Malchut, which is a very, very great measure, and all the more so in the first Partzuf of AK with which we are engaged, which comprises the whole difference from Ein Sof [infinity], which filled all of reality, to the Partzuf of AK, which is only the phase of a thin line of light relative to the light of Ein Sof. And know that this reflected light comprises all the surrounding light that is in all the worlds.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:8
items.html:
The reflected light that clothes direct light is an offspring of the first reflected light rejected from Malchut
And the second kind of reflected light included here is the reflected light that ascends from below upwards and clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light. And there is great depth in this. For in the reflected light rejected from phase four there is a phase of affirmation to be understood, that is, the substance of the light rejected from there; and there is a phase of negation to be understood in it, which is the force of the striking in itself, which gives birth to a great light by reason of the separation from the light. And this is a phase of shared relation between the light rejected backwards and phase four, which remains empty of that light. And this reflected light, born by reason of the separation from the light, is the reflected light of the second kind, which ascends and clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light. And therefore it is reckoned an offspring of the reflected light of the first kind mentioned above, since it is principally from the phase of negation, but by way of a shared relation, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:9
items.html:
The two kinds of reflected light are inner light and surrounding light; a great difference between HB TM of the inner light
Now the two kinds of reflected light mentioned above are discerned as the inner light and the surrounding light of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head]. For that reflected light which clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light is a very small part of the totality of the reflected light rejected backwards, since it is only an offspring and a phase of shared relation between the vessel of Malchut and the rejected light. And you already know that there are four phases of direct light, one above the other, called HB, ZA, and Malchut, and Keter [crown] is their root, and the difference between them is very great and mighty. And therefore the offspring born from a phase of shared relation of the rejected light with the phase of Malchut is not like that born from a shared relation of the rejected light with the phase of ZA, and all the more so with the phases above ZA.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:10
items.html:
Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida (NRNHY) are born and emerge from the shared relation of the rejected reflected light with KHB TM of direct light
And from what has been explained you will understand the birth of the five lights called Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya and Yechida. For that which is born from a shared relation of the reflected light with the phase of Malchut is called the light of Nefesh; and that which is born from a shared relation of the reflected light with the phase of ZA is called the light of Ruach; and that which is born from the reflected light and the phase of Bina is called the light of Neshama; and that which is born from the reflected light with the phase of Hochma is called the light of Haya; and that which is born from the reflected light and the phase of Keter [crown] is called the light of Yechida.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:11
items.html:
If the clothing reflected light is an offspring of a shared relation of the rejected reflected light with Malchut, the light is discerned as the light of Nefesh
And now, since the reflected light that clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light was an offspring of the reflected light with the phase of Malchut, the light drawn inside these ten Sefirot is called the light of Nefesh. And it is the inner light of these ten Sefirot, and the totality of the rejected reflected light is the surrounding light of these ten Sefirot. Now the two kinds of reflected light have been explained.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:12
items.html:
The third reflected light is that which is clothed in the Malchut of the Rosh [head], which is source and Keter [crown] both for the ten Sefirot of reflected light in the Rosh and for the ten Sefirot in the Guf [body]
The third kind of reflected light is the reflected light that remains fixed and enduring in the Malchut of the Rosh, in the phase of a source and Emanator for all the lights and the vessels that are in the Guf. For there is nothing in the Guf that is not drawn from that source; for since Malchut, by the quantity of reflected light that she raises, clothes all the lights of the Rosh, as above, she is thereby reckoned as a phase of Keter and root, both for the lights of the Rosh and for the lights of the Guf. For there is no grip at all upon light without a vessel; and since it is she who gives birth to the reflected light that clothes the lights, she is therefore reckoned as though she had given birth to the lights themselves as well.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:13
items.html:
The fourth reflected light expands from the Peh [mouth] to the Tabur, and becomes vessels for direct light, though not complete ones
The fourth kind is the reflected light that broadens the vessel of Malchut into ten Sefirot from herself and within herself, from above downwards, which is termed “from the Peh to the Tabur.” For the Malchut of the Rosh [head] is termed the Peh, and the Malchut of the Guf [body], which is the tenth Sefira of the Malchut of the Rosh, is called the Tabur. And in truth this reflected light becomes actual vessels for the ten Sefirot of direct light that descend within it from above downwards; and for this very reason these ten Sefirot are called by the name “the Guf of the Partzuf.” Only they are not recognized as such, and that is because of the great importance of the coarseness in it, as written in the Inner Light (Chapter 6, Item 5).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:14
items.html:
The fifth reflected light is the reflected light in the Malchut of the Guf [body], which is called Tabur
The fifth kind is the reflected light in the Malchut of the Guf, which is called female light, and which is in truth an illumination of direct light — only it is a small illumination, in which there is only a phase of reception, without any force of bestowal, and therefore it is called by the name reflected light. And remember this.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:15
items.html:
The sixth reflected light is that which expands from the Tabur downwards
The sixth kind of reflected light is all that expands from the Tabur downwards in the Guf [body], and all of it is only the phase of the Malchut of the Guf. For of the ten Sefirot that expand from the Peh [mouth] to the Guf, the first nine Sefirot end at the Tabur, and the Malchut among them occupies all this place, which is from the Tabur to the Sium of the Partzuf. And although she is Malchut alone, nevertheless she is discerned in herself as expanding into ten Sefirot; and that is by reason of the phase of the Sium of each and every Sefira that is discerned in this place.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:16
items.html:
What emerges in the coupling by striking in the Rosh [head] is discerned only in the Guf [body]. The expansion down to Malchut is discerned from the Peh [mouth] to the Tabur, and the rejection from Malchut is discerned from the Tabur downwards
And you must understand here that we have no grasp whatsoever of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, since they are the phase of Ein Sof [infinity], and all that we discern in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh is only from the aspect of their expansion into the Guf — and from the lower one the upper is learned. And therefore, when we say that the upper light expanded down to Malchut, and the screen in the vessel of Malchut struck the light and did not let it come into the vessel of Malchut and returned it backwards, and that this reflected light clothed the ten Sefirot of direct light — this clothing of the first nine Sefirot, and this rejection from expanding into Malchut, are discerned by us for the reason that they are so enacted in the Guf at the Tabur: for the first nine Sefirot that are found from the Tabur upwards are found received and clothed within the reflected light, whereas the light that belongs to the Sefira of Malchut is rejected and is not received in the Malchut of the Guf, which is the whole place from the Tabur downwards. And since this Malchut, while she was in the phase of Ein Sof before the restriction, clothed all the ten Sefirot — and for that very reason the light filled all of reality, as written at length in the Inner Observation (Part 1, Chapter 1 and Chapter 2), see there — therefore we likewise discern in the Malchut that was restricted, that is, in the place from the Tabur downwards, that there remained in her ten spaces that were emptied of the light they had had while they were in the phase of Ein Sof, and in which there is now nothing but reflected light alone. And therefore we discern in the Malchut of the Guf ten Sefirot in their own right, since they bear all the deficiency that appeared by reason of the restriction. Understand this well. And for this reason that place from the Tabur downwards is called by the name posterior, because of the lack of direct light; and the place from the Tabur upwards is called by the name the anterior of the Partzuf, because it is the place of all the light that is in the Partzuf, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:17
items.html:
The seventh reflected light is that which remains in the Partzuf after the departure of the direct light from it
The seventh kind is the reflected light that remains below in the Guf [body] after the departure of the direct light from there, which is brought in the ARI’s words (Chapter 2, Item 10). For when the direct light returns upwards to its root, the reflected light does not ascend with it; for the whole essence of reflected light is a light of departure, as was explained above, Item 8, since it is from the aspect of the separation of phase four, which does not receive the light — and this is by force of the restriction and of the screen mounted upon her, which is discerned as coarseness and judgment according to its origin. Only, at the hour when it becomes a vessel that draws and clothes the upper light, this coarseness and judgment are reversed and become complete refinement and mercy, until it is not recognized at all as low and dim relative to the upper light clothed within it, as above in Item 14. Indeed, at the hour of the departure, when the upper light expanded away from it and ascended to its root, its importance lapsed from it, and there remained of it no more than what it is according to its own essence, that is, coarseness and restriction and judgment, as above. And by this it is understood that at the time of the departure, when the direct light returned to its root, the reflected light could not ascend upwards with it; on the contrary, for now its descent downwards was revealed, that is, the judgment and the coarseness in it were revealed as it is according to its own essence, as above. And because of this it is called coarse light. And from now on the difference is discerned retroactively between the vessels that clothed the light, that is, the reflected light, and the light clothed in it — which was not recognized at all before the departure, as above in Item 13. And this is what the ARI says there, that this coarse light is the phase of the vessels of the Partzuf.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:18
items.html:
The eighth reflected light is the aforesaid reflected light after it attained coarseness additional to its own coarseness
The eighth kind is the aforesaid reflected light, from the aspect of its reception of coarseness additional to the coarseness it has of itself, as in the ARI’s words (Chapter 6, Item 2). For besides the coarseness that was revealed in it, that which it is according to its essence, there was further added in it the impression of a new judgment that it attained through the present departure, which left it in darkness, so that because of this it is found in a doubled thickening.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:19
items.html:
The ninth reflected light ascends from the coupling by striking upon the screen in the degrees of its refinement
The ninth kind is the reflected light that ascends by a coupling by striking made upon the screen in the degrees of its refinement; and the levels that emerge in these couplings are reckoned in their totality as reflected light — even the direct light in them — for the reason that these couplings emerge at a time of judgment, that is, at the hour of the departure of the lights to the Emanator.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:20
items.html: And one should not object that in each and every level there is an expansion of direct light from above downwards into the Guf [body], and that everything drawn from above downwards is mercy, as is known. The matter is that in truth there is nothing more here than the matter of refinement alone; and even these couplings that are made by the upper light are likewise included under the phase of the departure of the lights, because such is the way of refinement — for it is necessary that it pass and come through the four phases on its way of refinement, and the upper light, which does not cease even for a moment, is found coupling with it along its way. And this is like a man who goes out of the house: although he takes, for example, four steps on his way out of the house, nevertheless we do not reckon them as though they were four halts in the middle of his walking, and this would not enter the mind at all, for it is impossible for him to leave the house except by way of steps, since that is the way of walking. So is the matter before us: although at the time of the departure the screen passes through four phases, and the upper light couples with it along its way, nevertheless this is not reckoned as a phase of expansion of the upper light into the Partzuf from the aspect of mercy, but is reckoned as a phase of judgment; for the time is a time of departure, which includes also the expansions along its way, because such is the ordinary way of departure. And remember this.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:21
items.html: Now it has been explained that although in each and every coupling that emerges at the time of the refinement of the screen there is a complete level of Rosh [head], Toch and Sof [end], nonetheless they are not reckoned as direct light and mercy, but as reflected light and judgment, as explained. Indeed, all this is said with respect to the self of the Partzuf in general, which suffers from the departure of the lights from within it, and which therefore does not so greatly esteem the levels that emerge in the course of the refinement and the departure of the light. Not so when we reckon with the values of the levels, that is, from the aspect of their particularity in their own right: from those levels the inverse value comes out for us, for every level that emerges by a coupling nearer to the Emanator is the more excellent (in the manner explained in Items 9 and 10, see there). For in phase four only the light of Nefesh emerged, and when it was refined to phase three the light of Ruach emerged, and when it was refined to phase two the light of Neshama emerged, etc.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:22
items.html: And the matter of the inverse value mentioned above must be understood well, with absolute clarity, for it is the whole connection and the whole distinction between light and vessel; and therefore the lack of knowledge of it will trip us at every span and step in the course of the wisdom before us. The matter is that there is a phase of vessel of reception for the upper light from the side of direct light, which are the five phases KHB ZON, or Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida (NRNHY); and there is a vessel of reception from the side of reflected light, which are the levels that are likewise called KHB, ZA and Malchut. And they are inverse to one another from one extreme to the other: for from that very coupling in which the level of Keter [crown] of the reflected light emerges, that is, the greatest vessel, there emerges the phase of Nefesh of direct light, which is the smallest light, as brought above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:23
items.html: Now the source of these two values has already been explained: for the value of the four phases of direct light is drawn thus from the light of Ein Sof [infinity], where the first three phases are still not reckoned as a vessel of reception, because the discernment of disparity of form is not yet recognizable in them, and the whole difference between them and the upper light is only in this, that they cause the cascading of phase four, which is the phase of complete reception, as is known. And therefore every more refined phase is discerned as the greater, because it has more adhesion with the upper light clothed in it. And therefore Keter [crown], which is the more distant cause of phase four, is the root of the whole expansion. And phase one, which is a cause nearer to phase four than Keter, is reckoned as a light smaller than Keter; for besides being an effect and a consequence of Keter, there is found in it also a phase of the slightest fine change from the light clothed in it, namely in that it is a second cause and nearer to phase four. And likewise phase two, which is a third cause and nearer to phase four, so the light clothed there is found smaller still, and so on in this way, until phase four herself is found entirely without light, because of the disparity of form in her, upon which the restriction took place. All this is known from the preceding parts, and there is no need to elaborate.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:24
items.html: Now the differing values of the phases mentioned are called by the names Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida, and the difference between them is very great. And the principal difference is from the side of nearness to and distance from phase four, upon which the force of the restriction rests, as above. There is a further difference between them, of cause and consequence, in that Keter [crown] is the cause of Hochma, and Hochma of Bina, etc. And the superiority of the cause over the consequence that issues from it is very, very great in spiritual things, and it bears no likeness or comparison to the meaning of cause and consequence in corporeal terms; for here they are all eternal, and all the lights attained by the consequence must pass to it by way of its cause. And moreover, the principal part of this passing light is found to remain in the cause, and only the phase of a small branch of it is bestowed and comes to the lower one, the consequence that issues from it, although the light belongs only to the consequence. And there are many further discernments, such that the distance between the cause and the consequence that issues from it is infinitely great. And besides all this, there is a great difference in these four phases according to the kind of the light in itself; and although the upper light is all in one equality, indeed there is here a matter of shared relation between the upper light and the phase of direct light that is clothed within it. For the light of Haya is the phase of self, and the light of Neshama is principally the light of Hassadim, and there are further differences that will be explained in their place.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:25
items.html: And know that all the values stated above in the four phases of direct light are drawn thus from Ein Sof [infinity], and by reason of their coming to illuminate from the restriction downwards. And all these discernments stated hold likewise in the ten Sefirot of circles, and that is because they come thus from Ein Sof before their entry into the coupling by striking and the clothing of the reflected light. And you already know that the whole distinction between the ten Sefirot of circles and the ten Sefirot of straightness is only in the matter of the coupling by striking, which does not hold in the circles.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:26
items.html: And now we shall explain the second value, that is, the five levels of reflected light, which is an entirely different matter. And it has already been explained in Part 2, in the Inner Observation (Chapter 6), that from the restriction downwards the reflected light became a vessel of reception for the upper light in the place of phase four, as written there (Chapter 2). For that reflected light rejected from Malchut, which Malchut does not receive because of the restraint in the screen, becomes a vessel and a receptacle for the light, just as phase four was in Ein Sof [infinity]; and no light is received in the worlds except by way of the reflected light, as written there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:27
items.html: And therefore, if the coupling by striking is made upon the screen of phase four — she who was the principal receptacle in Ein Sof [infinity], for she clothed there all the light, which is up to Keter [crown], this being the secret that the light filled all of reality — therefore now, when all this great measure has been rejected from her and has risen upwards in the secret of reflected light, this reflected light too is found clothing the light in its full height, that is, up to Keter. And if indeed it is refined to phase three within her, and the measure of phase four in her is concealed from there, then the screen that rejects the upper light from clothing in her rejects only the measure of three phases; for even had the light clothed in this vessel of phase three, it would have received from it only up to Hochma. And therefore the level of the rejected reflected light is likewise short, and clothes only up to Hochma, and so on in this way, as written there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:28
items.html: And just as the difference between Keter [crown] and Hochma of direct light is very, very great, as above, so exactly is the difference between the level of Keter and the level of Hochma of reflected light likewise infinite and beyond comparison. For although in reflected light the coarser is the greater, indeed this is said with respect to the vessel of drawing, that is, the screen and Malchut in which the coupling is made; whereas for the clothing of the light, the more refined vessels are needed, since it is necessary that the light have equivalence of form with the vessel. And the light that is greater among the phases of direct light is so for the reason that it is more refined (as above, in Item 22, see there); hence it is self-evident that when it comes to clothe in the vessel of reflected light, that vessel must become equal to it. And therefore it is necessary that if the level of reflected light reaches up to Keter, there is there a refined and clear vessel that is fit to clothe that great light of Keter; whereas in the level of phase three, whose level reaches only up to Hochma, the vessel that clothes the light of Hochma is of a station low beyond comparison relative to the vessel of Keter in the level of phase four, and so on in this way.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:29
items.html: And one should not object: if the coarseness of phase four was refined and only the coarseness of phase three remained, then it turns out that the phase of Malchut is concealed from there and only the first three phases remain — KHB and ZA — and so that level ought to have been shortened by Malchut, since that portion of reflected light is lacking there; why then was the reflected light shortened from clothing Keter [crown], a phase that is not lacking there? The matter is that it has already been explained in the Inner Observation in Part 2 (Chapter 9), the matter of the two courses that there are in the ten Sefirot: that the ten Sefirot of direct light are discerned from above downwards, and their opposite is the reflected light, which is discerned from below upwards; so that below, in the place of the Malchut of direct light, is found the Keter of reflected light, and in the place of the ZA of direct light is found the Hochma of reflected light, and so on, until in the place of the Keter of direct light is found the Malchut of reflected light, see there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:30
items.html: And with this you will understand the secret brought in Sefer Yetzira: “the end is lodged in the beginning and the beginning in the end,” which is brought in Etz Chaim (Gate 39, Discourse 15). For phase four, which is Malchut, is the end of the Sefirot, and by the striking of the upper light on the screen in her she draws into herself the light of Keter [crown], meaning that she binds it to illuminate in the Partzuf; and thereby she is found lodged literally in its beginning, that is, in Keter, which is the beginning of the Sefirot. And since Keter is drawn to the reflected light of phase four, all the ten Sefirot are drawn along with it, since Keter comprises them all. And therefore Malchut is reckoned as the Keter of reflected light, that is, the very measure of Keter; and phase three, which is called the ZA of reflected light and is second to her, is attributed only to the Sefira of Hochma, since it is second to the place of the coupling of the level of Keter and is refined by one degree, etc., until the Keter in her, which is fifth from the place of the coupling, is discerned only as Malchut. And so the phase of the end of direct light, which is the Sefira of Malchut, is found lodged in the beginning of the reflected light, which is the Keter of reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:31
items.html: And with this you will readily understand the objection that we raised: if it was refined to phase three, then only Malchut is lacking from here — why then was the reflected light shortened to such an extent that it can clothe not the level of Keter [crown], but only from Hochma downwards? And now this is well understood, for there is here an inverse value, in which phase four is reckoned here as Keter and phase three as Hochma, etc., in complete opposition to the direct light, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:32
items.html: Indeed, even so, one must also reckon with the measure of reception of direct light explained above (in Items 22 and 24, see there). For although the end is lodged in the beginning, and Malchut draws to herself the light of Keter [crown] and becomes the Sefira of Keter, as above, this does not mean that Malchut draws to herself the light of Yechida itself, for it is in no way possible that the light of Yechida should come through the drawing of the vessel of Malchut, but only through the drawing of the vessel of Keter of direct light. For how could that whole relation of the phases of direct light with the upper light clothed in them — drawn thus from Ein Sof [infinity], where the difference of higher and lower among them is great beyond comparison, as explained above (in Items 23 and 24) — be altered? Rather they are preserved with the utmost precision, and no phase shifts from the value of its station even slightly.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:33
items.html: Rather, the meaning of “the end is lodged in the beginning” is that the light of Nefesh of Malchut, which is attributed to her from the side of the direct light, grows and attains its own phase as it is included in Keter [crown]. For Keter comprises all the ten Sefirot down to Malchut, and the lights within them are discerned as the five parts of Yechida, which are called the Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida (NRNHY) of Yechida. And therefore the light of Nefesh of Malchut now attains her root that she has in Keter, which is called the Nefesh of Yechida; yet she attains nothing whatsoever above her own phase. And understand this.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:34
items.html: And you see that although there is an inverse value between the ten Sefirot of reflected light and the ten Sefirot of direct light, nevertheless they do not nullify or diminish one another in the slightest, for the one does not touch the other at all, even though they emerge at once from a single coupling. And from the coupling of phase four there emerges a level of ten Sefirot literally up to Keter [crown], yet only up to the Nefesh of Yechida. And from the coupling of phase three there emerge ten Sefirot in the level of Hochma, yet it does not attain of the phase of Hochma that is called Haya; for phase three is the phase of ZA, which is the light of Ruach of direct light, and the light of Hochma is drawn only by way of the Hochma of direct light, as above. Rather it attains its own phase as rooted in Hochma, which is called the phase of the Ruach of Haya. And so it is with all of them, that each one draws and attains only its own phase in the direct light, but the level of reflected light causes it to take its phase from a higher place, according to the measure of the level.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:35
items.html: And one should not object according to this: how is it possible that the light of Ruach, whose value exceeds that of Nefesh beyond comparison, as above (in Items 23 and 24), is found clothing in a level lower than that of the light of Nefesh? For the light of Nefesh is drawn by phase four and clothes in the level of Keter [crown], while the light of Ruach, which must be drawn by phase three, is found clothing only in the level of Hochma, which is much lower than the level of Keter. Indeed, in truth, in the world of correction, when the vessels have been corrected as they should be, it is always found that although the light of Ruach is drawn by phase three, nevertheless it clothes only in the level of Keter; for then Nefesh descends from the level of Keter and clothes in the level of phase three, and the light of Ruach clothes in the level of Keter. And so it is with all of them, as written in Part 2 in the Inner Observation, see there. But here, before the vessels were corrected, since they emerged here only by way of refinement, when phase three emerged and drew the light of Ruach, the vessel of the level of Keter was already not in existence, for the screen had already departed from there; therefore it was compelled to come and clothe in a vessel lower than the vessel of Nefesh, and because of this the Partzuf could not receive from it the full measure of its illumination.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:36
items.html:
The tenth reflected light is that which descends from the four levels that emerge in the refinement of the screen into the empty vessel beneath them
The tenth kind is the reflected light that descends from the four levels that emerge in the refinement of the screen, from the place of the coupling downwards into the vessel beneath it that is empty of light; and it is brought in the ARI’s words here (Chapter 4, Item 3). For at the time when phase four was refined to phase three, when the light departed from phase four and the level of Keter [crown] was concealed, and the coupling was made in phase three and the level of Hochma emerged — then the reflected light descends from the illumination of the coupling in phase three and comes into the vessel of phase four, which is empty of her own light. And likewise, when the place of the coupling departed from phase three and rose to phase two, and phase three too was emptied of its light, the illumination of the coupling descends from phase two into the empty vessel of phase three, and so on in this way.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:37
items.html:
In this reflected light there are two deficiencies: the first, that it comes from the refinement of the screen, which is judgment; the second, that it is drawn from below the Tabur
Now this reflected light has two deficiencies. The first is that it comes from a coupling made at the time of refinement, and because of this the whole of that level is reckoned as a phase of reflected light and judgment, as above in the eighth kind of reflected light. And the second deficiency is that it is drawn from a phase below the Tabur; for when the screen is refined to phase three, the Malchut of the Rosh [head] ascends to the Hotem [nose], and then the Hotem is reckoned as the Peh [mouth] of the Rosh, from which the light descends and expands from above downwards into the Guf [body] as far as phase three of the Guf, which is now reckoned as the phase of Malchut of the Malchut of the Rosh, which is called the Tabur. And likewise when it is refined to phase two, phase two of the Guf is discerned as the phase of the Tabur, and so on in this way. And therefore the reflected light that descends from the illumination of the coupling of phase three of the Guf to phase four of the Guf is discerned as coming below the Tabur. And it has already been explained that this reflected light is the phase of posterior and judgment, as above in Items 15 and 16, see there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:38
items.html:
The eleventh reflected light is the reflected light born of the striking of the record and the descending reflected light in one another, which is called sparks
The eleventh kind is the reflected light born through a coupling by striking of the record and the aforesaid descending reflected light in one another, brought in the ARI’s words here (Chapter 3, Item 9), where it is called the fourth light, see there. For the record and the reflected light, which are divided in their nature, strike one another, and through this sparks were separated from the aforesaid descending reflected light and came into the empty vessel below the place of the coupling.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 2:39
items.html:
The twelfth reflected light is the aforesaid reflected light after the cessation of the coupling, when it darkens and is extinguished
The twelfth kind is that same reflected light of the eleventh kind mentioned above, only after they have been extinguished. For after the illumination of the coupling ceased from phase three, for example, there ceased with it also that illumination of the coupling which had been drawn from there into phase four; and therefore the sparks too, which had fallen and come into phase four, are found being extinguished, meaning that they have darkened from their illumination. And so likewise the rest of the sparks from the remaining phases.
